import pandas as pd

# File paths for source tables
source0_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length1_30/training_0.csv"
source1_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length1_30/training_1.csv"

# Load Source 0: ['userId', 'movieId', 'tag', 'timestamp']
# index_col=0 to ignore the numerical index column
df_source0 = pd.read_csv(source0_path, index_col=0)

# Load Source 1: ['movieId', 'title', 'genres']
df_source1 = pd.read_csv(source1_path, index_col=0)

# Join Source 0 and Source 1 on 'movieId' to get all columns required for target
# Target schema: ['movieId', 'title', 'genres', 'userId', 'tag', 'timestamp']
df_merged = pd.merge(df_source0, df_source1, on='movieId', how='inner')

# Reorder columns to match target schema exactly
df_target = df_merged[['movieId', 'title', 'genres', 'userId', 'tag', 'timestamp']]

# Ensure data types match target schema
df_target = df_target.astype({
    'movieId': 'int64',
    'title': 'string',
    'genres': 'string',
    'userId': 'int64',
    'tag': 'string',
    'timestamp': 'int64'
})

# Write the result to the target CSV file
output_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length1_30/target_multisource_cot.csv"
df_target.to_csv(output_path, index=False)

import pandas as pd

# Read source tables with index_col=0 to ignore the first numerical index column
source0 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length1_30/training_0.csv", index_col=0)
source1 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length1_30/training_1.csv", index_col=0)

# Join on movieId (inner join to avoid extra rows)
joined = pd.merge(source0, source1, on="movieId", how="inner")

# Group by the leftmost columns of the target schema except timestamp (which is FD dependent on movieId)
# According to FD, timestamp depends on movieId, but since userId, tag, timestamp are all in target,
# and userId and tag are not keys, group by movieId, title, genres, userId, tag and aggregate timestamp by max
grouped = joined.groupby(
    ["movieId", "title", "genres", "userId", "tag"], as_index=False
).agg({"timestamp": "max"})

# Write output with exact target schema column order
grouped = grouped[["movieId", "title", "genres", "userId", "tag", "timestamp"]]

grouped.to_csv(
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length1_30/target_multisource_critique_history.csv",
    index=False,
)
